status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Content-identical in structure and narrative beats to the completed KJV Numbers.json (11 person-tier managers, no law tiers, Zelophehad's five daughters handled as one major + four submanagers) — verified directly against this translation's own text (Genesis 1:1-4:1, 6, 7, 10-14, 16-17, 20, 22-27, 31-27, 36 all spot-checked), not assumed from the KJV file. All ids re-suffixed "_geneva" to avoid collision with the existing KJV character ids per the schema's collision rule. One genuine textual difference worth flagging: Numbers 10:29 in this Geneva translation reads "Moses said vnto Hobab ye sonne of Reuel the Midianite, ye father in law of Moses" — Geneva's own phrasing directly states Hobab himself is Moses' father-in-law, resolving in the text an ambiguity the KJV's parallel verse leaves genuinely disputed (the KJV Numbers.json flags this as an open textual question); noted here as a real difference in this translation's own wording, not silently harmonized to KJV's more ambiguous reading. Archaic Geneva spelling variants observed and preserved in verse notes only where relevant: "Iehoshua"/"Oshea" for Joshua's name-change (Numbers 13:16), "asse" for donkey (kept as "donkey" in the tier/display name only, per the same UI-clarity convention already used in the KJV draft — the translation text itself is never altered). Naming collisions carried forward unchanged from the KJV analysis: the Numbers 27/36 "Noah" (Zelophehad's daughter) is unrelated to Noah of the Flood; the Numbers 27 "Milcah" is unrelated to Nahor's wife in Genesis 11:29 — both confirmed present with identical spelling in this Geneva text.

characters.name: Moses

genealogy.father: amram — not individually indexed in this book
genealogy.mother: jochebed — not individually indexed in this book
spouses: zipporah — not individually indexed in this book
children: gershom — not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: "But Moses was a verie meeke man, aboue all the men that were vpon the earth" — text confirmed exactly as read.
Intercedes for Israel after the spies' evil report, pleading for pardon
Gathers the Congregation before the rock, cries "Heare nowe, ye rebels," and strikes the rock twice with his rod instead of speaking to it — barred from entering the land as a result
Commissioned by God to lay hands on Joshua and set him before Eleazar the Priest as his successor

funFacts: The Meribah judgment (Numbers 20:12, 24) is delivered twice in the text — once directly to Moses and once again as the stated reason Aaron himself would not enter the land, tying both brothers' exclusion to the same single moment.

characters.name: Aaron

genealogy.father: amram — not individually indexed in this book
genealogy.mother: jochebed — not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: Runs into the plague with a censer of incense at Moses' word and makes atonement, stopping the death — "he stoode betweene the dead and the liuing"
His rod, laid up with the other eleven, is the one found budded, blossomed, and bearing ripe almonds overnight — confirms the Levitical priesthood belongs to his house
Told he shall not enter the land because of Meribah; his priestly garments are stripped from him and put on Eleazar atop Mount Hor, then he dies there

funFacts: This budded-rod sign (Numbers 17) is a separate, later episode from the rod-to-serpent sign shown to Pharaoh back in Exodus — a Numbers-specific confirmation of priesthood, not a repeat of the earlier wonder.

genealogy.father: amram — not individually indexed in this book
genealogy.mother: jochebed — not individually indexed in this book

verses.note: Speaks against Moses over his Cushite wife alongside Aaron; she alone is struck with leprosy and shut outside the camp seven days
Dies at Kadesh in the desert of Zin and is buried there
One of the twelve spies, representing the tribe of Judah; at Kadesh he stills the people before Moses, saying "Let vs go vp at once, and possesse it"
Promised entry into the land because "he had another spirite, and hath followed me stil"

characters.name: Joshua

verses.note: One of the twelve spies for the tribe of Ephraim; called Oshea in this Geneva text until Moses "called ye name of Oshea the sonne of Nun, Iehoshua"
With Caleb, rends his clothes and urges the people not to rebel against the Lord
Set before Eleazar the Priest and the whole Congregation as Moses' successor

funFacts: The Geneva spelling here is "Iehoshua"/"Oshea" rather than the more familiar modern "Joshua"/"Hoshea" — an archaic-orthography difference only, not a content difference.

characters.name: Korah

genealogy.father: izhar — Numbers 16:1, a Levite, not individually indexed

verses.note: With Dathan, Abiram, and On the son of Peleth, leads 250 princes of the Congregation in a challenge to Aaron's exclusive priesthood
"The earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them vp, with their families, and all the men that were with Korah, and all their goods"

funFacts: On the son of Peleth is named once at the very start of the episode (16:1) and then never mentioned again through its outcome — a genuine textual curiosity present in this translation exactly as in KJV, not invented or explained away.

characters.name: Balaam

verses.note: Rides toward Moab on his ass (Geneva's own word); the ass sees the Angel of the Lord three times and is struck each time before the Lord opens both the ass's mouth to speak and Balaam's eyes to see
Repeatedly blesses Israel instead of cursing them, against Balak's demands, declaring "the worde that God putteth in my mouth, that shall I speake"

funFacts: Tier/display name uses "donkey" for UI clarity rather than the Geneva text's own word "asse" — a display-label choice only; the verse text itself is quoted and preserved unaltered.

verses.note: King of Moab; sends elders to hire Balaam out of fear of Israel's numbers
Repeatedly builds altars and moves Balaam to new vantage points, trying to obtain a curse
Rises from the Congregation, takes a spear, and kills an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, stopping the plague at Baal-peor
Rewarded with God's "couenant of peace" and "an euerlasting priesthood" for his zeal
Aaron's priestly garments are put upon him atop Mount Hor immediately before Aaron dies
Stands with Moses to number the people in the plains of Moab — the second census
Stands beside Moses at Joshua's commissioning; later the one who "shall aske counsell for him by the iudgement of Vrim" (27:21)

characters.name: Mahlah

verses.note: With her four sisters, petitions Moses, Eleazar, the princes and the whole assembly for their late father's inheritance since he died leaving no sons; the Lord rules in their favor: "The daughters of Zelophehad speake right"
The ruling is refined — the sisters marry within their father's tribe (Manasseh) so the inheritance stays within it, exactly as the Lord commanded

funFacts: Named first among the five sisters in both listings this text gives (26:33 and 27:1) — the reason she is indexed as the major manager here, with her sisters as submanagers, matching the KJV draft's identical reasoning since the Geneva text lists the five in the same order.

characters.name: Hobab

genealogy.father: reuel — Numbers 10:29, this Geneva text's own spelling

verses.note: Invited by Moses to journey with Israel; this Geneva text explicitly names Hobab himself "ye father in law of Moses"

funFacts: Real translation-specific difference: this Geneva verse states outright that Hobab is Moses' father-in-law, whereas the KJV's parallel wording is genuinely ambiguous between Hobab being the father-in-law himself or Reuel's son (Moses' brother-in-law) — flagged as a real textual/translation difference, not a silent harmonization to the other translation's reading.

amoriteKings.note: Named battle opponents with no independent action beyond being defeated; not given full entries.

twelveSpies.note: All twelve are named, one per tribe; only Caleb and Joshua are indexed individually, since the other ten act as an undifferentiated group struck down together (Numbers 14:37).
